authors_or_organization: Society for Corporate Governance (Randi Morrison blog); report with Board Intelligence

authors_or_organization: Entergy Services, LLC

limitations: Abstract only. Observational audit of 1618 randomly sampled reports in one (large) system; four cancer types; measures format use and element documentation, not downstream effects.

title: Mandatory second opinion surgical pathology at a large referral hospital
authors_or_organization: Kronz JD, Westra WH, Epstein JI (Johns Hopkins)
url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10590387/ (Cancer 1999;86(11):2426-2435); abstract read via Europe PMC REST API
limitations: Abstract only (PubMed page blocked by cookie wall; Europe PMC abstract used). Changed diagnosis defined narrowly (excludes grade/stage changes), so underestimates all discrepancies; no adjudication against outcomes described in abstract; single referral center; data ~30 years old.

title: Mandatory second opinion in surgical pathology referral material: clinical consequences of major disagreements
authors_or_organization: Manion E, Cohen MB, Weydert J (University of Iowa)
url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18360282/ (Am J Surg Pathol 2008;32:732-737); abstract read via Europe PMC REST API
limitations: Abstract only. Single institution; disagreement classified by the second-opinion pathologist (who is not a neutral arbiter); clinical follow-up used for significance.

title: Impact of neuroradiologist second opinion on staging and management of head and neck cancer
authors_or_organization: Lysack JT, Hoy M, Hudon ME, Nakoneshny SC, Chandarana SP, Matthews TW, Dort JC
limitations: Retrospective, non-blinded; 94 cases, single center; pathologic gold standard only for 30 surgical cases; second readers had more clinical information and knew the context; time/cost of re-reads not measured.

title: Reducing the rate of repeat imaging: import of outside images to PACS
authors_or_organization: Lu MT, Tellis WM, Fidelman N, Qayyum A, Avrin DE (UCSF)
limitations: Abstract only. Retrospective observational, 267 patients before chemoembolization at one center; small 'not available' group (n=18); adjusted ORs but residual confounding possible (e.g., why images were not imported).

title: 40 CFR Part 312 - Innocent Landowners, Standards for Conducting All Appropriate Inquiries (7-1-20 edition)
authors_or_organization: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Code of Federal Regulations, via GovInfo)
limitations: Regulation shows required report content and user duties, not compliance, report quality, or whether data-gap disclosure changes buyer behavior. ASTM E1527-21 (the practice most Phase I reports follow) could not be accessed (astm.org returned 403; standard is paywalled).

title: BI-RADS lexicon for US and mammography: interobserver variability and positive predictive value
authors_or_organization: Lazarus E, Mainiero MB, Schepps B, Koelliker SL, Livingston LS
limitations: Abstract only. 5 radiologists, 94 biopsied lesions (enriched sample), single center, BI-RADS 4th edition; authors interpret agreement as 'good' despite fair kappa for final category.

title: Structured Head and Neck CT Angiography Reporting Reduces Resident Revision Rates
authors_or_organization: Johnson TF, Brinjikji W, Doolittle DA, Nagelschneider AA, Welch BT, Kotsenas AL (Mayo Clinic)
data_collection_dates: not reported in abstract (2-month template period)
limitations: Abstract only. Resident-driven QI project; very small structured group (17 reports); revisions are attending corrections of resident preliminary reports (producer-side rework), mostly typographical per authors; trade-press summaries report inconsistent baseline counts (10/41 vs 11/54) - abstract figures used.
